en.title: JPMorgan Chase OA #1: Range Negation Updates
en.description:
A data analyst has an array data of length n representing data for n days. He performs k updates in order; each update is [l, r], meaning every element from index l to r (inclusive, 1-indexed) is negated (x becomes −x).

Find the array after all updates are done.
en.input:
The first line contains an integer n, and the second line contains n integers data[1..n]. The third line contains an integer k, followed by k lines with two integers l r each.

1≤n≤10^6, 1≤k≤10^6, |data[i]|≤10^9, 1≤l≤r≤n.
en.output: Output one line with the n integers of the final array, separated by spaces.
en.explanation:
Example 1: after the first update [2,4] the array is [1,4,5,−2], and after the second update [1,2] it is [−1,−4,5,−2].
Example 2: after [1,3] it is [−1,−2,−3,4,5], and after [2,4] it is [−1,2,3,−4,5].
Example 3: applying [1,3] twice changes nothing, and then the 2nd element is negated; negating 0 still gives 0.
hints: Negating twice leaves a value unchanged, so you only need the parity of how many times each position is covered.
For range [l,r], XOR 1 into the difference array at both l−1 and r.
Take prefix XORs from left to right, and negate wherever the result is odd.
